overview: This event ties together electrical system, avionics malfunctions, and lost communications in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

items.text: Loss of airspeed, altimeter, VSI on PFD. Affects gear warning, TAD, transponder Mode C. Use BFI.

children.text: It uses electrical buses (fused circuit hubs) to isolate and organize electrical loads.
A bus tie system connects the forward and aft cockpit buses for redundancy and efficiency.
Circuit protection is provided by circuit breakers in both cockpits.
Monitoring and fault protection include voltage sensors and annunciator lights.

items.text: Not all circuit breakers are accessible in flight (hot bus)

children.text: Approximately midway between the Waldron Shrimp Ponds and Chapman Ranch
Minimizes impact to populated areas and air traffic corridors while maximizing SAR and aircraft reclamation effectiveness.

items.text: Make all calls in the blind

children.text: Try multiple radios/frequencies (UHF, VHF, Backup, manual entry)

studyNotes.summary: Have Electrical System and Avionics Malfunctions organized before step so the cockpit workload never outruns the brief.
